h1: The 8 Best Printers for College Students of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best printers for college students, covering inkjet, laser, and portable options for dorm rooms and shared apartments.
summary: The HP DeskJet 4355 is the best printer for college students who do not yet know their workload: print, scan and copy for $50 to $100 with a 3-month Instant Ink trial. The Canon TS4320 adds duplex for color work, the Brother HL-L2405W suits text-heavy majors, and the Canon TR4720 handles scanning.
intro: Sticker price is the wrong number to shop by in a dorm. A $50 inkjet that burns through cartridges during finals week costs more per page than a laser that cost twice as much, and the student who prints a hundred pages of readings feels it first, usually at the worst moment. Before you compare models, decide what you actually print: essays, color posters, or scanned problem sets.

We reviewed eight printers on paper, comparing technology, duplex, auto document feeders, mobile printing and how well each fits a cramped desk. The ranking rewards versatility for mixed coursework first, then lets specialists win their niche, so a general-education student and a law major can land on different answers from the same list, and neither is wrong.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The most flexible compact printer for a general student.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 is a wireless color inkjet that prints, scans and copies from a compact body, and it comes with a 3-month Instant Ink trial. Instant Ink bills by pages printed, not by cartridge, which softens the early cost for a student who prints in bursts. Its price tier is $50 to $100.

It takes first place because it covers every basic need without specializing in one. The Canon TS4320 adds duplex but is aimed at color-heavy work, and the Brother laser gives up scanning and color entirely. This is the printer to buy before your major sets the demands.

Buy it if you are undeclared or print a mix of essays and the odd color page. The caveat is running cost: inkjet cartridges add up over a semester, and the listing shows no duplex, so long readings cost double the paper. Skip it if you print hundreds of text pages monthly.
products.idealFor: Undeclared or general education students with mixed needs.
products.skipIf: You print hundreds of text pages a month.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Duplex printing makes it the best pick for visual coursework.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is a wireless color inkjet that prints, copies and scans, and it adds automatic duplex so a long reading uses half the paper. A 1-year limited warranty comes with it, and the price tier is $50 to $100. Color matters here because art, design and architecture students print mockups and proofs that need accurate output on every page.

It takes second place because duplex saves paper on long readings, a feature the HP DeskJet lacks. The HP wins overall only because its Instant Ink trial and broader appeal edge it out. Against the TR4720 below, the TS4320 trades the document feeder for two-sided printing.

Buy it if you are in a visual major or print in color weekly. The caveat is the same inkjet running cost as the HP, and no document feeder, so scanning a stack means lifting the lid each time.
products.idealFor: Art and design students who print in color.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A black-and-white laser for students who print a lot of text.
products.description:
The Brother HL-L2405W is a compact monochrome laser with wireless and mobile printing and Alexa support. It also includes a Refresh Subscription trial. Laser toner does not dry out the way inkjet cartridges do when a printer sits idle between assignments, and toner pages generally cost less than ink when the volume is high. It is priced at $100 to $200.

It ranks third because it is print-only. The inkjets above also scan and copy, and two of them print in color, which makes them more flexible for a first dorm printer. Where the laser wins is volume: a law, business or humanities student who prints PDFs by the stack gets cheaper black text than any inkjet here.

Buy it if you read mostly on paper. The caveat is blunt: no color, no scanning, no copying. Skip it if any of those matter.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An auto document feeder for multi-page scanning.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TR4720 is the scanning specialist, with an auto document feeder, wireless and mobile printing, and print, scan, copy and fax functions. A feeder lets you drop a multi-page problem set or a signed lease on the tray and scan it in one pass, instead of lifting the lid for every page. Price tier is $50 to $100.

It ranks fourth because the feeder is a real advantage for multi-page work, but students rarely need fax, and the TS4320 offers duplex that this model does not list. Against the HP DeskJet, the feeder is the entire reason to pay attention to this one, since the basics are the same.

Buy it if you scan paperwork often, such as signed forms, receipts or handwritten notes. The caveat is that fax is an unused extra, and duplex is missing, so skip it if you only print.
products.idealFor: Students who scan many pages or signed documents.
products.skipIf: You only print and never scan.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: A light, basic printer for occasional printing.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA TS3720 is the basic option: a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with a compact, lightweight body that prints, scans and copies. Its weight matters in a dorm that gets packed up each semester, and the simple controls suit someone who prints a handful of pages a week. The price tier is $50 to $100.

It ranks fifth because it has no duplex, no document feeder and no trial ink plan, so it offers less than the four picks above. The HP DeskJet 4355 and Canon TS4320 sit in the same price tier with a trial or duplex. What the TS3720 keeps is a low profile and basic wireless printing.

Buy it for light printing needs and a small desk. The caveat is that it does not stand out in any feature, so every page costs the same inkjet premium. Skip it if you print long readings or scan stacks.
products.idealFor: Students with light, general printing needs.
products.skipIf: You want duplex or a feeder.

products.name: Canon Pixma MG3620 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Mobile and tablet printing suits locked-down laptops.
products.description:
The Canon PIXMA MG3620 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with mobile and tablet printing support, in a black compact body. Printing from a phone or tablet bypasses the driver installs that school-issued Chromebooks and restricted laptops often block. It prints, scans and copies, and sells in the $100 to $200 tier.

It ranks sixth because it costs more than the TS3720 and TS4320 yet adds no feature beyond mobile printing. If your laptop is unrestricted, you pay extra for something you will not use. If it is locked down, that mobile path is the reason to pick it, and the HP and Canon picks above are less certain to work.

Buy it if your laptop blocks driver installs. The caveat is a higher price for modest specs, and no duplex is listed. Skip it if value for money leads.
products.idealFor: Students with a Chromebook or restricted laptop.
products.skipIf: You want the best value for the money.

products.name: Inkless Portable Printer for Travel (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: No ink or toner, but it only does thermal prints.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is a Bluetooth inkless thermal printer that handles 8.5 by 11 inch Letter and A4 at 300 DPI. It uses heat on special paper, so there are no ink or toner cartridges to dry out or replace. It works with iOS, Android and laptops, and the price tier is $50 to $100.

It ranks seventh because thermal output is monochrome and it does not scan or copy, so it replaces a full printer only for light use. Against the Brother laser, which is also black-and-white only, it gives up volume and print quality but needs no consumables. The tradeoff is zero ink cost for a narrow job.

Buy it if you mostly use library printers and need an occasional page at your desk. The caveat is that thermal paper is its own ongoing cost and output type is limited. Skip it for scanning or regular color prints.
products.idealFor: Students with very light printing needs.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or regular color prints.

products.name: Canon TS6420 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A fuller control panel for shared use.
products.description:
The Canon TS6420 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one in a black compact body, with a fuller control panel layout than the simpler Canon models. It prints, scans and copies, and it sits in the $100 to $200 tier, above the TS4320. A proper panel helps when several people use one printer and need to reach copy or scan quickly without opening an app.

It ranks last because its spec sheet lists no standout feature beyond that panel. The TS4320 gives you duplex for less, and the TR4720 gives you a document feeder. For a single student, the extra money buys convenience, not capability.

Buy it if you split a printer with roommates and want a panel everyone can use. The caveat is the higher price tier for few listed extras. Skip it if you are buying alone on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You are buying alone on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: Inkjets print color and photos well, but cartridges run out and dry up with disuse. Laser printers use toner and suit lots of black text, and toner does not clog during idle weeks. Decide based on whether you print color and how much text you print. The listing names the technology in the title, so check it before comparing prices.

Duplex means automatic two-sided printing, which halves paper use on long readings and makes thick packets easier to carry. Many cheap printers lack it, and the HP DeskJet lists none. Look for the word duplex or auto two-sided on the spec sheet, not just in marketing copy. Without it you must flip pages by hand.

An auto document feeder scans a stack of pages without lifting the lid for each one. That saves real time on problem sets, contracts and signed forms. Check the listing for ADF or auto document feeder, as the Canon TR4720 lists. A flatbed alone makes multi-page scanning a slow, page-by-page chore.

School Chromebooks and locked laptops often block driver installs, so a USB or driver-based printer may not work at all. Mobile printing support lets you print from a phone, tablet or browser instead. Look for wireless and mobile or tablet printing in the bullets, as the Canon MG3620 lists, and ask your IT office what is allowed.

Purchase price is only part of the cost, since ink or toner is the rest, and it often exceeds the printer after a year. Trials like Instant Ink can help early on. Check which cartridges the model uses, how many pages they print, and whether a subscription fits your volume before deciding.

howToChoose.note: Most students should default to inkjet unless they print mostly black text in volume.

faq.q: Does a printer work with a Chromebook?
faq.a: Many do via wireless and mobile printing. The Canon MG3620 lists mobile and tablet support, which helps on locked-down laptops. Confirm compatibility on the listing and with your school's IT office before buying, because a locked laptop can block wired and driver setups.

faq.q: What mistake do students make buying printers?
faq.a: Buying on sticker price alone. A cheap inkjet like the Canon TS3720 can cost more per page than a laser once ink is counted. Match the technology to what you print before comparing prices, and count ink as part of the cost.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: Only if you print lots of black text. The Brother HL-L2405W is a laser but cannot do color, scanning or copying. Light or mixed users do better with the HP DeskJet 4355.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless printer?
faq.a: Connect it to your Wi-Fi from the control panel or app, then add it to your laptop or phone. Dorm networks sometimes restrict this, so ask your IT office. The HP DeskJet 4355 and Canon models all use wireless setup.

faq.q: How do I keep inkjet ink from drying?
faq.a: Print something short every week or two, since long idle gaps let inkjet cartridges clog. That applies to the HP, Canon and Brother inkjets alike. A laser like the Brother HL-L2405W is far more forgiving of long idle stretches.

faq.q: Can I rely on a portable thermal printer?
faq.a: For occasional black pages, yes. The MT610Pro prints at 300 DPI on Letter and A4 with no ink, but it does not scan or copy and the output is monochrome. Keep a full printer for anything else, especially forms you must scan.

finalTake: Buy the HP DeskJet 4355 if you are undeclared or print a mix, the Canon TS4320 for color and paper savings, and the Brother HL-L2405W if your major means stacks of black text. The TR4720 wins for scanning, and the MT610Pro suits a student who mostly uses library printers. Match the technology to the workload before anything else.
